Clothes & getting dressed

pyjamas noun

also pajamas, pyjama, pajama

modern

Traupman 117

synthesis dormītōria

Classically synthesis is a set of clothes or a loose dinner gown (Mart.).

Examples

  • Theodōrus, synthesī dormītōriā etiamtum indūtus, in sellā altā sedēbat

    Theo, still in his pyjamas, was sitting in his high chairFābula III, Apud avum et aviam

See also nightclothes.

SourcesLewis & Short: synthesis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 117, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater: Fābulae Latīnae ad vītam cotīdiānam I–VII, as revised on 29 October 2026. Examples marked “Fābula” quote those texts word for word.
